title: Shake a Leg
label: Relentless
format: CD single (RELCD22, per 45worlds); OCC lists a further catalogue number RELDX22, format not stated

type.basis: Evidence specimen; a pop single built on a salsa-quoting sample, filed as pop by a 2005 trade sheet and as grime by sources on its album.

sound.text: Built on a sample of 'Mambo Craze' by De Phazz featuring Pat Appleton (45worlds sleeve notes; Wikipedia; Record of the Day, 2005).
Record of the Day (2005) calls it summer fun and pop, but 'smart and witty'.
PopMatters (2006) hears the salsa-quoting hook as reminiscent of 'Mambo No. 5'.

context.text: Official Singles Chart peak no. 24 (first chart date 22/10/2005, 5 weeks); no. 18 on the Physical Singles Chart and no. 31 on Downloads (OCC).
Record of the Day (Oct 2005) notes it ranked seventh on the pre-release airplay chart despite a modest midweek chart position.
Simon Reynolds (Spin, 2005) wrote that the parent album 'skimps on uncut grime' in favour of conventional hip hop and novelty tunes.

uncertainty: OCC catalogue RELDX22 differs from the 45worlds CD RELCD22; probably a second format, not confirmed. 45worlds gives only 'October 2005'.
tracklist: CD single: 1. Shake A Leg (Radio Edit); 2. Heat Up. Track 1 lyrics credited to Wiley, Breeze and Scratchy; track 2 lyrics to Jet Le, Breeze, Scratchy, Trim and Flow Dan (45worlds). Taken from the album In at the Deep End (Relentless/Virgin, 6 June 2005).

audit.note: Single not listed on the artist page; parent album page shows 'Rock · 2005', ℗ 2005 Universal Music Operations Limited (15 songs; track list not visible, so the track's presence is not confirmed on Apple). A 'Shake a Leg' music video is listed on the album page.
Read from the artist discography listing: Relentless/Virgin, 1 Jan 2005 (likely placeholder date). Also 'Shake A Leg (Radio Edit)' (Hip-Hop/Rap). On Qobuz the album In At The Deep End is Hip-Hop/Rap.
